system.summary: Latin clear text with a two-part nomenclator of 3-4 digit groups (some with 1/2) and letter signs (Lq Rex Sueciae, aa cum, rr et, t in), and words spelled with numbers 10-99, three homophones per letter in consecutive blocks (15-17 s, 18-20 m, 21-23 f, 24-26 e, 27-29 l, 30-32 r, 36-38 x, 39-41 q, 45-47 d, 48-50 c, 51-53 i, 54-56 p, 57-59 w?, 60-62 u, 63-65 o, 66-68 h, 69-71 b, 72-74 a, 75-77 g, 78-80 n, 81-83 t); nulls 10, 11, 88-90, 95, 97-99.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear glosses on the glossed letters (existing). Image 442 is a bare duplicate whose glossed original is on 438-440 (found 13 Nov 2026, after the code-list test); 426 likewise has its glossed original on 425. No edition of these letters found (searches of 6 Nov 2026, catalogue row 2313 vetting n09); not on DECODE; no target for this volume in the repository (origin/main f6b285a7b, 13 Nov 2026). Not opened: F. H. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955) and Stålhane 1934 ('Camerarius key'); Riksarkivet Chifferklaver I:19 A and I:22 not digitised.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (pre-registration, frozen keys and transcriptions, one measurement per test, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the letter table and the code list, ran the tests and wrote up; a separate agent did the blind second transcription pass and another the blind judging. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Letter table learned from the glosses of images 409, 414, 423, 427, frozen.
Held-out image 498: 83 glossed letters, 0.904 against 0.277 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (thresholds 0.85 and +0.30).
Code groups and glosses of images 402, 405, 406, 412, 415, 418, 419 added to those of 414, 423, 427, 498: 109 groups (codes.tsv), frozen.

Held-out image 442 (unglossed), transcribed after the freeze in two passes: blind forced choice between the list's value and a random decoy for the 59 covered code occurrences, 59/59 against 0.695 for the best of 200 random controls (thresholds n >= 30, 0.85 and +0.30). 4 items had an empty filler by a clean-up flaw; without them 55/55 against 0.673.
Image 442 read with key.tsv and codes.tsv: 335 of 414 word units read by sense (0.81).

Glossed original 438R/439R/439L/440L and glossed letter 444R transcribed in two passes (second blind, 613 of 636 cipher elements agreed), arbitrated on the image: 158 code-gloss pairs, 116 new groups or signs (codes_438-444.tsv).

Glossed original 439 aligned with the held-out duplicate 442: 352 of 361 cipher elements identical; the glosses of 439 agree with codes.tsv for all 59 occurrences judged in the blind test (51 same word, 8 synonym or same referent). Post hoc check, not a new measurement.
Image 442 read with the glosses of its original: 415 of 420 word units (0.988), reading_442_v2.md.

Integration check: own decoder from key.tsv and the two code lists on transcription_442.txt reproduces the spelled words and code values of decryption_442_v2.txt; 442R compared with the Riksarkivet image (full/max): about 110 cipher elements agree (7/3 as declared); glosses of 439R lines 1-18 agree with reading_442_v2.md; strict recount 402/420 = 0.957 (contributor 0.988); camerarius1621 code compared: 6 shared groups, all with different values (separate key); class set to read in part (bare letters 432, 460, 454 open), method to read from existing decipherment.

outcome.method_basis: Every text read here carries a decipherment of the time: the glossed letters on their own leaves, and image 442 through its glossed original on 438-440 (found 13 Nov 2026, after the code-list test). The letter table and the code list were learned from the glosses of other letters and passed the contributor's held-out tests (498, 442), but no letter without a decipherment of the time has been read yet (432, 460, the postscript on 454).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py): letter table 0.904 vs 0.277 on image 498; code list 59/59 vs 0.695 (blind forced choice) on image 442. Integration check 14 Nov 2026: the hashes, scripts, decoys and judge files are not in the repository, so 'frozen before' is by the contributor's record; 442 turned out to be the bare duplicate of the glossed 438-440, so the held-out text had a decipherment of the time (not used by the test, by the contributor's record).

texts.label: image 442, postscript and end of the letter of 20/30 Sept 1630 (duplicate of 438-440)
texts.summary: Frederick Henry offers his help; Camerarius asks that Count Wilhelm's troops be kept (diversion or pay under the King's name) rather than disbanded into enemy hands; the States General defer; Neuburg has the Spanish led out of Juelich and seeks the same from the Emperor; the King should send orders and a soldier to take the companies into his service; a secret warning that the Prussian tolls are used to set Denmark against Sweden; intrigues against Camerarius.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences with the glosses of the original 438-440, aligned occurrence by occurrence; 5 code groups open; one AI reader, two transcription passes (second blind), no human review. docs/_check_reading.py on decryption_442_v2.txt: clean share 0.52 (names and period forms outside the word list). Integration check 14 Nov 2026: second decoder (own, from key.tsv) agrees on the spelled words; the strict share is 402/420 = 0.957 (probable units and the uncertain 'meam' are holes); 442R checked on the Riksarkivet image (about 110 elements agree, 7/3 confusions as declared) and the glosses of 439R top checked against reading_442_v2.md (all legible ones agree).
reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout

outcome.notes: The glossed letters were deciphered at the time; what is new is the letter table and the code list as validated reusable tables (now 225 groups). Image 442, first read as an unglossed held-out text, is a duplicate of the glossed 438-440: its content is existing. Not the 1621-22 Solms code of camerarius1621: the six code groups present in both lists all have different values (487, 722, 2095, 2472, 2503, 3143), so the two are separate entries (one key, one entry).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Image 442 (integration check 14 Nov 2026, README read bar, sure units only): 402/420 = 95.7%: the 403 units the contributor counts sure, less the spelled 'meam' (20.26.72.28, which the key decodes 'meal'; gloss 'nram' on the original; uncertain in both copies); the 12 probable and 5 unresolved units are holes. The contributor's figure, counting probable units: 415/420 = 0.988 (0.963 with the 11 probable nulls counted as unresolved). The bare letters 432, 460 and the postscript on 454 are not read; the target as a whole is read in part.
